#+TITLE: DIRECT Variant Surface — selection × partitioning × refinement control × hidden constraints
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: direct-variants

* Summary

The papers license a large, well-measured variant surface: three selection schemes (IO/IA/GL) × four partitioning schemes (N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP), plus refinement-control add-ons (epsilon, delta-limit, median/average, globally-biased, rev) and a hidden-constraint surrogate (DIRECT-GLh). For a 6-DOF search at 20k–35k evaluations, the literature says the current repo configuration — original-DIRECT selection with ε=0 and all ties, 1-DTC partition, L2 size — sits in the worst local-refinement regime; the highest-evidence upgrade is the GL (two-step Pareto) selection combined with 1-DTC or 1-DBDP partitioning, optionally with the globally-biased (-gb) phase switch for refinement control, and the GLh φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate if unrenderable poses produce NaN. The "restrictions hurt cheap functions" finding (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760) is real and worse when f_min ≈ 0 (the silhouette-cost shape), and -gb is indeed the only restriction that never hurt in that study — it was also the best on expensive functions. Every variant below can be expressed as an Options struct on DirectOptimizer with bit-identical defaults, and scored headlessly on a DIRECTGOLib/GKLS battery under the production cumulative-budget shape.

* Key Findings

** Finding 1: The repo's current configuration is the literature's worst-case local-refinement regime
- The extracted optimizer is original-DIRECT selection (Jarvis convex hull) with ε=0, selecting *all* hull points including equal-slope ties (`slope >= highest_slope`), trisecting one (largest denormalized) side, L2 size measure (norm of the side vector), center sampling. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L93-141, L143-200; /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/data_structures_6D.cpp L107-128]
- Jones & Martins 2021: "with ε=0 DIRECT spends so many evaluations refining local minima that it ends up far from the optimum after 3000 evaluations" (Shubert); the ε=0 regime allows "excessive local search". The ε|f_min| rule is what protects the original DIRECT from this — the repo has no such rule at all. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 (JOG 79:521–566, DOI 10.1007/s10898-020-00952-6), §3.3/Fig. 19]
- The empirical study's "IO" (improved original) scheme restricts ties to one candidate per (size,value) group; the repo selects all ties, which the study and Jones & Martins show increases "global drag" and slows convergence ("Best results are achieved by ignoring ties for potentially optimal rectangles, only trisecting on one side, and using Gablonsky's modified definition of rectangle size" — Figure 18). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §2.1.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §3.2]
- Confidence: high (code-verified against primary literature).
- Relevance: the 20k trunk budget is exactly the regime where ε=0 over-refinement wastes evaluations; tie-all selection adds drag on top. Both are cheap to fix (hull tie-break + optional ε filter) with bit-identical defaults preserved.

** Finding 2: GL selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems — the regime the 6-DOF search lives in
- On 96 DIRECTGOLib v1.1 box-constrained problems: GL-based variants failed 19/384 cases vs IO 63/384 and IA 55/384; GL required ~60% (vs IO) and ~62% (vs IA) fewer function evaluations overall, and ~72% fewer on n>4 problems. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.2]
- Budget-regime crossover (operational characteristics, n>4 multimodal): at ≤500 evals IO variants lead; at ~1000–4000 N-DTC-IO is best (~50% solved); at ≥4000 evals the GL variants (1-DTC-GL, 1-DBDP-GL) are the most efficient. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Fig. 7, §4.2]
- Partitioning for n>4: 1-DBDP-based variants best average (≈16% fewer evals than N-DTC-based); 1-DTDV "very inefficient for higher dimensional test problems"; 1-DTDV shines only when most solution coordinates sit on the boundary (ν≥8/10 coordinates: 551 evals vs 6,487 for N-DTC-IO on Levy10; but 141,999 vs 919 when interior). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.1, Table 3]
- On 800 GKLS problems (n=2–5, simple+hard classes): 1-DTC-IO best average (8,021) and best median (1,427); 1-DBDP-GL ranks 5th there but is best on simple classes at budgets >400 evals; IO wins on hard GKLS classes. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §5, Table 6]
- Confidence: high (directly from the study's tables; the study is the repo's own evidence base, papers/ 2022 PDF).
- Relevance: 6-DOF = n>4; 20k trunk = well above the 4000-eval crossover → GL selection is the evidence-backed choice; the partition choice is a tradeoff (1-DTC: best GKLS median + minimal change from current code; 1-DBDP: best n>4 average but requires diagonal-bisection rework). 1-DTDV is a trap unless the pose optimum is confirmed near the range boundary.

** Finding 3: The DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate is applicable to NaN/unrenderable poses at negligible cost
- GLh assigns infeasible midpoints the surrogate φ = f_min + d(x_min, x) (Euclidean distance in the *normalized unit cube*), normalized via f̄(x)=(f−f_min)/(f_max−f_min) and d̄=d/d_max so objective and distance are commensurate; f̄_min ≡ 0 drops out. Infeasible points never become f_min (min over feasible only). [Source: thesis §5.2, DOI 10.15388/vu.thesis.138 (mif.vu.lt PDF); DIRECTGO code /tmp clone Algorithms/sDirect_GLh.m Selection()]
- Cost is minimal: the distances d(x_min, x) are *already computed* for the GL two-step selection (the local step is Pareto on (size, distance)); per-iteration cost is one O(N) pass to re-tag infeasible values whenever f_min improves. "Such a technique does not require any additional computation." [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 (DIRECTGO, ACM TOMS 48(4), DOI 10.1145/3559755) §2.3; sDirect_GLh.m]
- Performance on hidden-constraint problems (constraint info withheld, 80 problems): DIRECT-GLh failed 18/80 vs DIRECT-NAS 29/80, DIRECT-Barrier 46/80, subDIRECT-Barrier 47–53/80; GLh took ~4.5× fewer iterations and ~33× less time than NAS. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §4.2.1, Table 5]
- DirectGO's own description of why alternatives fail: NaN-valued boxes "would not be selected as potential optimal at all"; barrier penalties leave feasible-edge exploration very slow. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §2.3]
- The repo currently passes NaN/Inf straight into storage: `EvaluateCostFunction` has no finite-check; a NaN result fails `result < current_optimum_value_` so it never becomes the optimum, but NaN boxes enter the storage matrix and poison hull slopes in `ConvexHull` (NaN slope comparisons). [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L203-220, L93-141]
- Confidence: high for the algorithm and cost; medium for *whether the production GPU silhouette cost actually emits NaN* — no NaN handling exists anywhere in the C++ cost path (only Qt UI validation in app/experimental/PoseBridge.cpp L177-184), so the trigger condition is unverified.
- Relevance: if the GPU cost can fail (degenerate poses, empty silhouette), GLh converts silent corruption into a directed search toward feasibility — and the needed distance data is already there once GL selection lands.

** Finding 4: Refinement control — "restrictions hurt cheap functions" is confirmed, and -gb is the only safe one
- Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760 tested six refinement-reduction add-ons on 1-DTC-GL over 287 DIRECTGOLib v1.2 problems: success rates 1-DTC-GL-gb 0.7840 (225/287) > 1-DTC-GL 0.7805 (224/287) > -limit 0.7631 > -min 0.7526 > -rev 0.7317 > -median 0.7073 > -average 0.6551. Every restriction except gb hurt the base algorithm; gb is "the only algorithm with the same or better performance than the original 1-DTC-GL". [Source: https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf Table 2, §3, §4]
- "In the case of cheap test functions, the original 1-DTC-GL is the best of all the algorithms tested, meaning that the local refinement reduction schemes are redundant. However, when the objective functions are expensive, the local refinement reduction techniques improve the performance, and 1-DTC-GL-gb is the best technique among all tested." [Source: same, §3–§4]
- The restriction harm is worst when f_min = 0: "the restriction on selecting small hyper-rectangles may prevent the algorithms from converging to a solution... especially apparent when the solution is equal to zero" (1-DTC-GL-average worsened average evals by 32% overall; suffered most on f*=0 problems). [Source: same, §3]
- gb mechanics (from the DIRECTGO implementation of the studied algorithm): run the traditional two-step selection; after 5 consecutive iterations without f_min improvement, drop the local (distance-based) selection phase, except every 5th iteration ("security" iteration) — `(fMinNotImpr > 5) && (mod(fMinNotImpr,5) ~= 0)` → local phase else global-only. Defaults `ovexpl='GL'`, `locbalance='GL'`, `ep=1e-4`. [Source: /tmp clone of https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO, Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m L122-138, L235-237; GENDIRECT parameter table in README]
- Jones & Martins: the ε=1e-4 default protects the original DIRECT from ε=0's excessive local search; adaptive-ε (Finkel-Kelley DIRECT-restart) is mixed (better on Shubert, worse on Powell-48). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §2.3.2, §3.3]
- Confidence: high (direct quotes from the study that owns this exact question).
- Relevance: JTML's silhouette cost has f_min ≈ 0 and a GPU eval that is expensive (dilation 6/3/1 renders) — the two conditions where restrictions fail and where gb pays. ε-based restrictions (min/median/average) are doubly contraindicated (window ε|f_min| collapses at f_min→0 — the Sergeyev–Kvasov zero-minimum weakness Jones & Martins reproduce). Answer to Q3: yes, -gb is the only refinement control that survives; for cheap analytic battery functions keep it OFF and test the crossover.

** Finding 5: The full variant surface maps onto an Options struct with bit-identical defaults
- The DIRECTGO toolbox exposes exactly this surface as options: `locbalance` ∈ {GL, gb, rev} and `ovexpl` ∈ {GL, min, median, average, limit} on the I_DTC_GL family; GENDIRECT generalizes to Partitioning{Strategy: DTC/DTDV/DTCS/DBVS/DBDP/DBVD/DBC, SubSides: All/One}, Selection{AggrFuncVal, CandMeasure: Diagonal/LongSide, Strategy: Original/Aggressive/Pareto/RedPareto, EqualCand: All/One, SolRefin: Min/Median/Average/Off, Ep: 1e-4, ControlEp: Off/Restart/MultiLevel1/MultiLevel2, GloballyBiased: Off/On, TwoPhase: Off/On}. [Source: https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO README, GENDIRECT table; Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m header]
- The 12 studied variants are the cross-product IO/IA/GL × N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP; N-DTC-GL ≡ DIRECT-GL; 1-DBDP-GL ≡ GL-selected BIRECT; the study's IO and BIRECT/DIRECT differ only in the tie restriction. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §3, Table 1]
- Repo mapping: selection mode → `ConvexHull()` (L93-141; add ε post-filter, tie restriction, Pareto front, aggressive), split rule + sampling → `TrisectPotentiallyOptimal()` (L143-200; currently 1-DTC-alike: one side, largest denormalized, center sampling — a coincidence worth pinning), size measure → `HyperBox6D::size_` (L107-128; L2 norm of sides; Gablonsky L∞ = half longest side is the alternative), hidden constraints → `EvaluateCostFunction()` (L203-220) + a feasibility flag in `DirectDataStorage`, budgets → already parametric (`budget_` + `SetCallOffset`, Run() L30-67; settings_constants.h TRUNK_BUDGET=20000, BRANCH_BUDGET=5000×2, Z_SEARCH_BUDGET=5000).
- Defaults must reproduce today's bit-identical search: selection=original-ε=0-all-ties, split=1-DTC-largest-denormalized-side, size=L2, hidden=off — every new Options field defaults to current behavior (R13 pin).
- Confidence: high (code + DIRECTGO source verified).
- Relevance: the harness (angle 03) can then score variants by swapping one Options value; defaults unchanged means the Tier-1/Tier-2 golden gates still hold for the baseline config.

** Finding 6: The analytic battery exists in the papers and is headless-portable
- DIRECTGOLib v1.1: 96 box-constrained problems, n ∈ {2,5,10}, known f*, domains; includes Hartman6 (n=6, f*=−3.3223), Goldstein-Price (n=2, f*=3.0), Shekel 5/7/10 (n=4), and n=5 variants of Ackley/Alpine/Griewank/Rastrigin/Rosenbrock/Schwefel/Levy/Michalewicz/Styblinski-Tang — the last being the closest analytic stand-in for 6-DOF pose search. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Appendix A Table 7; library at https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGOLib, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6491951]
- GKLS: 8 classes × 100 instances, n ∈ {2,3,4,5}, simple+hard (r or d adjusted); stopping by distance-to-optimum accuracy Δ (eq. 10), budget 1e6 in the study. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §5, Table 5; generator: Gaviano et al., ACM TOMS 29(4):469–480, 2003, DOI 10.1145/962437.962444]
- Scoring convention in the papers: percent-error stop pe = 100·(f−f*)/|f*| (pe=f for f*=0) with ε_pe=1e-2, plus operational-characteristics/data profiles (proportion solved vs budget) — the exact tool for the 20k/35k production budget question. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4; arXiv:2107.02205 §4]
- The repo already has the headless pattern: test/unit/test_direct_optimizer.cpp runs analytic costs (quadratic in 6-D) through DirectOptimizer with budgets 1000–20000, determinism/offset/callback assertions — the natural skeleton for the battery harness. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/test/unit/test_direct_optimizer.cpp]
- Confidence: high.
- Relevance: the battery spec below is the hand-off to angle 03 (harness owner); this angle owns the variant surface + function/budget/termination choices, not the harness implementation.

* Variant Surface (12 + refinement add-ons)

** Selection schemes
- IO — Improved Original: lower-right convex hull of (size, f(center)) with ε in eq. (4), ties restricted to one candidate per (size,value) group. Current repo = this *without* ε and *with* all ties.
- IA — Improved Aggressive: select the min-value box of every distinct size group, with δ_limit floor (in the study: box subdivided 50n times). Parallel-friendly; worst sequential record in the 2022 study.
- GL — two-step Pareto: step 1 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, f(center) ↓); step 2 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, Euclidean distance from x_min ↓); union. No ε, no parameters; "does not have any protection against over-exploration in sub-optimal local minima regions".

** Partitioning schemes
- N-DTC — trisect *all* longest sides at once (2k+1 new evals per POH, k = # of max sides); original DIRECT (Jones 1993).
- 1-DTC — trisect the single longest side only (2 evals per POH); tie-break in the study: least-split-so-far dimension, then lowest index. Repo is 1-DTC-alike but ties break by *denormalized* side length (GetLargestDirection on denormalized sides), lowest index on equality — for anisotropic ranges (branch 15,15,25,25,25,25; leaf 3,3,15,3,3,3) the two rules diverge.
- 1-DTDV — trisect single longest side, sample two *diagonal vertices*; boundary-optimum weapon; catastrophic on interior optima / high n.
- 1-DBDP — bisect along the diagonal, sample two interior diagonal points (reusable across descendants); best n>4 average; needs its own storage/diameter bookkeeping.

** Refinement-control add-ons (on top of GL, per Mathematics 2022)
- -min / -median / -average: ε-style floors f_min−ε|f_min|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_median|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_average| — all hurt, worst at f*=0.
- -limit: δ_limit floor (20n subdivisions in the 2022 paper) + always select the f_min box — hurt slightly (0.7805→0.7631 success).
- -gb: globally-biased two-phase switch (drop local phase after 5 non-improving iterations, security iteration every 5th) — the only non-hurting restriction; best on expensive functions.
- -rev: local phase only on the iteration f_min improves — mixed (best median, 5th success rate).
- ε=0 default in the repo vs ε=1e-4 in DIRECTGO defaults: keep 0 (current behavior) for the analytic battery baseline; the ε>0 option exists for the original-selection regime.

* Per-variant evidence (headline numbers)

| Variant | DIRECTGOLib avg evals / failed | GKLS avg / median | Notes |
|---------+--------------------------------+-------------------+-------|
| N-DTC-IO (≈ repo, but ε=1e-4, no ties) | worst-of-IO family; IO failed 63/384 overall | (IO family) | wins only at ≤500-eval budgets [arXiv:2109.14912 §4.2, Fig. 7] |
| N-DTC-GL | GL family: ~60–72% fewer evals than IO/IA on n>4 | 5th (24,746 avg) | ≡ DIRECT-GL [arXiv:2109.14912 §3] |
| 1-DTC-IO | IO family; best ≤400 evals | best avg 8,021, best median 1,427 | best on hard GKLS [arXiv:2109.14912 §5] |

| 1-DTDV-* | best on n≤4, boundary optima (Deb02: 2 evals vs 77+); 141,999 evals on interior Levy10 | 3rd best avg 15,231 | avoid unless boundary confirmed [arXiv:2109.14912 §4.1.1, Table 3] |
| 1-DBDP-GL | best n>4 average (≈16% fewer than N-DTC) | 2nd on simple GKLS at >400 evals; 5th overall | ≡ BIRECT with GL selection [arXiv:2109.14912 §4.1, §5] |
| 1-DTC-GL-gb | 0.7840 success (225/287); only non-hurting restriction | — | the refinement-control survivor [epublications.vu.lt PDF] |

  - ConvexHull() L93-141 — selection mode switch (original/IO/GL/IA), ε post-filter, tie restriction, Pareto two-step (needs d(x_min,x): reuse GetDistanceFrom on unit coords), δlimit floor.
  - TrisectPotentiallyOptimal() L143-200 — split-rule switch (1-DTC default / N-DTC / 1-DTDV / 1-DBDP) and sampling scheme; currently 2 evals per POH on the largest *denormalized* side (1-DTC-alike).
  - EvaluateCostFunction() L203-220 — finite check; NaN/Inf → mark infeasible; GLh surrogate values applied at selection time (f_min + d(x_min,x), normalized by (f_max−f_min) and d_max=√n).
  - DenormalizeRange() L222-230 / DenormalizeFromCenter() L232-246 — unit↔physical; the GLh distance must be computed in *unit* coordinates (matches DIRECTGO's MSS.CC).

  - f*=0 subset (Ackley/Alpine/Griewank/Rastrigin/Rosenbrock/Schwefel/Levy/Sphere): mirrors the silhouette f_min≈0 shape — must be reported separately, since the papers show restrictions hurt most here.
  - GKLS: 8 classes × 100 instances (n=2,3,4,5; simple + hard) with distance-to-optimum stopping (eq. 10, Δ per class).
- Budgets/termination (production shape):
  - Flat: 20000 (trunk-only) and cumulative 20000/25000/30000/35000 via SetCallOffset to reproduce the 3-stage cascade headlessly.
  - Crossover probe: 100, 500, 1000, 4000 to confirm the IO→GL regime switch at the exact shapes (papers: IO ≤500, N-DTC-IO ~50% @ 1000–4000, GL ≥4000).
  - Scoring: percent-error stop pe ≤ 1e-2 (f*≠0) / pe=f (f*=0), plus operational-characteristics (proportion solved vs budget) and median-evals-to-solve — same metrics as the papers, so results are directly comparable.

* Recommended default variant for the production budget shape

- Landing variant: **1-DTC-GL-gb** — 1-DTC partition (already the repo's de-facto split rule), GL two-step Pareto selection (n>4, ≥4000-eval regime: ~60–72% fewer evals than IO/IA), locbalance=gb (only refinement control that never hurt; best when evals are expensive — GPU silhouette with dilation 6/3/1). Keep size measure L2 and ε=0 (bit-identical default; no ε-style restrictions — f_min≈0 makes them harmful).
- Stretch variant: 1-DBDP-GL (best n>4 average; needs diagonal-bisection rework of storage/sampling).
- Do not enable 1-DTDV unless the battery (shifted-domain + boundary probes) shows the pose optimum near the range edge; evidence shows it is catastrophic for interior optima.
- Enable the GLh φ-surrogate only if the GPU cost can emit NaN/Inf — this angle could not verify the trigger; that check belongs to angle 02's cost-path audit. If NaN is possible, GLh turns it from silent storage corruption (hull slope NaN) into a feasibility-directed search at near-zero extra cost.
- Ordering per the measurement-first rule: land Options struct with bit-identical defaults first (Tier-1 + Tier-2 gates must stay green on the baseline config), then score 1-DTC-GL vs 1-DTC-GL-gb vs 1-DBDP-GL vs baseline on the battery above; no variant touches production until the harness says so.

(4) is used but does not state ε in the fetched text; DIRECTGO's default ep=1e-4 is the presumable value (marked medium confidence). This matters for how "current repo vs N-DTC-IO" is interpreted — the repo uses ε=0.

#+TITLE: DIRECT Variant Surface — selection × partitioning × refinement control × hidden constraints
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: direct-variants

* Summary

The papers license a large, well-measured variant surface: three selection schemes (IO/IA/GL) × four partitioning schemes (N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP), plus refinement-control add-ons (epsilon, delta-limit, median/average, globally-biased, rev) and a hidden-constraint surrogate (DIRECT-GLh). For a 6-DOF search at 20k–35k evaluations, the literature says the current repo configuration — original-DIRECT selection with ε=0 and all ties, 1-DTC partition, L2 size — sits in the worst local-refinement regime; the highest-evidence upgrade is the GL (two-step Pareto) selection combined with 1-DTC or 1-DBDP partitioning, optionally with the globally-biased (-gb) phase switch for refinement control, and the GLh φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate if unrenderable poses produce NaN. The "restrictions hurt cheap functions" finding (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760) is real and worse when f_min ≈ 0 (the silhouette-cost shape), and -gb is indeed the only restriction that never hurt in that study — it was also the best on expensive functions. Every variant below can be expressed as an Options struct on DirectOptimizer with bit-identical defaults, and scored headlessly on a DIRECTGOLib/GKLS battery under the production cumulative-budget shape.

* Key Findings

** Finding 1: The repo's current configuration is the literature's worst-case local-refinement regime
- The extracted optimizer is original-DIRECT selection (Jarvis convex hull) with ε=0, selecting *all* hull points including equal-slope ties (`slope >= highest_slope`), trisecting one (largest denormalized) side, L2 size measure (norm of the side vector), center sampling. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L93-141, L143-200; /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/data_structures_6D.cpp L107-128]
- Jones & Martins 2021: "with ε=0 DIRECT spends so many evaluations refining local minima that it ends up far from the optimum after 3000 evaluations" (Shubert); the ε=0 regime allows "excessive local search". The ε|f_min| rule is what protects the original DIRECT from this — the repo has no such rule at all. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 (JOG 79:521–566, DOI 10.1007/s10898-020-00952-6), §3.3/Fig. 19]
- The empirical study's "IO" (improved original) scheme restricts ties to one candidate per (size,value) group; the repo selects all ties, which the study and Jones & Martins show increases "global drag" and slows convergence ("Best results are achieved by ignoring ties for potentially optimal rectangles, only trisecting on one side, and using Gablonsky's modified definition of rectangle size" — Figure 18). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §2.1.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §3.2]
- Confidence: high (code-verified against primary literature).
- Relevance: the 20k trunk budget is exactly the regime where ε=0 over-refinement wastes evaluations; tie-all selection adds drag on top. Both are cheap to fix (hull tie-break + optional ε filter) with bit-identical defaults preserved.

** Finding 2: GL selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems — the regime the 6-DOF search lives in
- On 96 DIRECTGOLib v1.1 box-constrained problems: GL-based variants failed 19/384 cases vs IO 63/384 and IA 55/384; GL required ~60% (vs IO) and ~62% (vs IA) fewer function evaluations overall, and ~72% fewer on n>4 problems. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.2]
- Budget-regime crossover (operational characteristics, n>4 multimodal): at ≤500 evals IO variants lead; at ~1000–4000 N-DTC-IO is best (~50% solved); at ≥4000 evals the GL variants (1-DTC-GL, 1-DBDP-GL) are the most efficient. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Fig. 7, §4.2]
- Partitioning for n>4: 1-DBDP-based variants best average (≈16% fewer evals than N-DTC-based); 1-DTDV "very inefficient for higher dimensional test problems"; 1-DTDV shines only when most solution coordinates sit on the boundary (ν≥8/10 coordinates: 551 evals vs 6,487 for N-DTC-IO on Levy10; but 141,999 vs 919 when interior). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.1, Table 3]
- On 800 GKLS problems (n=2–5, simple+hard classes): 1-DTC-IO best average (8,021) and best median (1,427); 1-DBDP-GL ranks 5th there but is best on simple classes at budgets >400 evals; IO wins on hard GKLS classes. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §5, Table 6]
- Confidence: high (directly from the study's tables; the study is the repo's own evidence base, papers/ 2022 PDF).
- Relevance: 6-DOF = n>4; 20k trunk = well above the 4000-eval crossover → GL selection is the evidence-backed choice; the partition choice is a tradeoff (1-DTC: best GKLS median + minimal change from current code; 1-DBDP: best n>4 average but requires diagonal-bisection rework). 1-DTDV is a trap unless the pose optimum is confirmed near the range boundary.

** Finding 3: The DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate is applicable to NaN/unrenderable poses at negligible cost
- GLh assigns infeasible midpoints the surrogate φ = f_min + d(x_min, x) (Euclidean distance in the *normalized unit cube*), normalized via f̄(x)=(f−f_min)/(f_max−f_min) and d̄=d/d_max so objective and distance are commensurate; f̄_min ≡ 0 drops out. Infeasible points never become f_min (min over feasible only). [Source: thesis §5.2, DOI 10.15388/vu.thesis.138 (mif.vu.lt PDF); DIRECTGO code /tmp clone Algorithms/sDirect_GLh.m Selection()]
- Cost is minimal: the distances d(x_min, x) are *already computed* for the GL two-step selection (the local step is Pareto on (size, distance)); per-iteration cost is one O(N) pass to re-tag infeasible values whenever f_min improves. "Such a technique does not require any additional computation." [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 (DIRECTGO, ACM TOMS 48(4), DOI 10.1145/3559755) §2.3; sDirect_GLh.m]
- Performance on hidden-constraint problems (constraint info withheld, 80 problems): DIRECT-GLh failed 18/80 vs DIRECT-NAS 29/80, DIRECT-Barrier 46/80, subDIRECT-Barrier 47–53/80; GLh took ~4.5× fewer iterations and ~33× less time than NAS. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §4.2.1, Table 5]
- DirectGO's own description of why alternatives fail: NaN-valued boxes "would not be selected as potential optimal at all"; barrier penalties leave feasible-edge exploration very slow. [Source: arXiv:2107.02205 §2.3]
- The repo currently passes NaN/Inf straight into storage: `EvaluateCostFunction` has no finite-check; a NaN result fails `result < current_optimum_value_` so it never becomes the optimum, but NaN boxes enter the storage matrix and poison hull slopes in `ConvexHull` (NaN slope comparisons). [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp L203-220, L93-141]
- Confidence: high for the algorithm and cost; medium for *whether the production GPU silhouette cost actually emits NaN* — no NaN handling exists anywhere in the C++ cost path (only Qt UI validation in app/experimental/PoseBridge.cpp L177-184), so the trigger condition is unverified.
- Relevance: if the GPU cost can fail (degenerate poses, empty silhouette), GLh converts silent corruption into a directed search toward feasibility — and the needed distance data is already there once GL selection lands.

** Finding 4: Refinement control — "restrictions hurt cheap functions" is confirmed, and -gb is the only safe one
- Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760 tested six refinement-reduction add-ons on 1-DTC-GL over 287 DIRECTGOLib v1.2 problems: success rates 1-DTC-GL-gb 0.7840 (225/287) > 1-DTC-GL 0.7805 (224/287) > -limit 0.7631 > -min 0.7526 > -rev 0.7317 > -median 0.7073 > -average 0.6551. Every restriction except gb hurt the base algorithm; gb is "the only algorithm with the same or better performance than the original 1-DTC-GL". [Source: https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf Table 2, §3, §4]
- "In the case of cheap test functions, the original 1-DTC-GL is the best of all the algorithms tested, meaning that the local refinement reduction schemes are redundant. However, when the objective functions are expensive, the local refinement reduction techniques improve the performance, and 1-DTC-GL-gb is the best technique among all tested." [Source: same, §3–§4]
- The restriction harm is worst when f_min = 0: "the restriction on selecting small hyper-rectangles may prevent the algorithms from converging to a solution... especially apparent when the solution is equal to zero" (1-DTC-GL-average worsened average evals by 32% overall; suffered most on f*=0 problems). [Source: same, §3]
- gb mechanics (from the DIRECTGO implementation of the studied algorithm): run the traditional two-step selection; after 5 consecutive iterations without f_min improvement, drop the local (distance-based) selection phase, except every 5th iteration ("security" iteration) — `(fMinNotImpr > 5) && (mod(fMinNotImpr,5) ~= 0)` → local phase else global-only. Defaults `ovexpl='GL'`, `locbalance='GL'`, `ep=1e-4`. [Source: /tmp clone of https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO, Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m L122-138, L235-237; GENDIRECT parameter table in README]
- Jones & Martins: the ε=1e-4 default protects the original DIRECT from ε=0's excessive local search; adaptive-ε (Finkel-Kelley DIRECT-restart) is mixed (better on Shubert, worse on Powell-48). [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150 §2.3.2, §3.3]
- Confidence: high (direct quotes from the study that owns this exact question).
- Relevance: JTML's silhouette cost has f_min ≈ 0 and a GPU eval that is expensive (dilation 6/3/1 renders) — the two conditions where restrictions fail and where gb pays. ε-based restrictions (min/median/average) are doubly contraindicated (window ε|f_min| collapses at f_min→0 — the Sergeyev–Kvasov zero-minimum weakness Jones & Martins reproduce). Answer to Q3: yes, -gb is the only refinement control that survives; for cheap analytic battery functions keep it OFF and test the crossover.

** Finding 5: The full variant surface maps onto an Options struct with bit-identical defaults
- The DIRECTGO toolbox exposes exactly this surface as options: `locbalance` ∈ {GL, gb, rev} and `ovexpl` ∈ {GL, min, median, average, limit} on the I_DTC_GL family; GENDIRECT generalizes to Partitioning{Strategy: DTC/DTDV/DTCS/DBVS/DBDP/DBVD/DBC, SubSides: All/One}, Selection{AggrFuncVal, CandMeasure: Diagonal/LongSide, Strategy: Original/Aggressive/Pareto/RedPareto, EqualCand: All/One, SolRefin: Min/Median/Average/Off, Ep: 1e-4, ControlEp: Off/Restart/MultiLevel1/MultiLevel2, GloballyBiased: Off/On, TwoPhase: Off/On}. [Source: https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGO README, GENDIRECT table; Algorithms/I_DTC_GL.m header]
- The 12 studied variants are the cross-product IO/IA/GL × N-DTC/1-DTC/1-DTDV/1-DBDP; N-DTC-GL ≡ DIRECT-GL; 1-DBDP-GL ≡ GL-selected BIRECT; the study's IO and BIRECT/DIRECT differ only in the tie restriction. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §3, Table 1]
- Repo mapping: selection mode → `ConvexHull()` (L93-141; add ε post-filter, tie restriction, Pareto front, aggressive), split rule + sampling → `TrisectPotentiallyOptimal()` (L143-200; currently 1-DTC-alike: one side, largest denormalized, center sampling — a coincidence worth pinning), size measure → `HyperBox6D::size_` (L107-128; L2 norm of sides; Gablonsky L∞ = half longest side is the alternative), hidden constraints → `EvaluateCostFunction()` (L203-220) + a feasibility flag in `DirectDataStorage`, budgets → already parametric (`budget_` + `SetCallOffset`, Run() L30-67; settings_constants.h TRUNK_BUDGET=20000, BRANCH_BUDGET=5000×2, Z_SEARCH_BUDGET=5000).
- Defaults must reproduce today's bit-identical search: selection=original-ε=0-all-ties, split=1-DTC-largest-denormalized-side, size=L2, hidden=off — every new Options field defaults to current behavior (R13 pin).
- Confidence: high (code + DIRECTGO source verified).
- Relevance: the harness (angle 03) can then score variants by swapping one Options value; defaults unchanged means the Tier-1/Tier-2 golden gates still hold for the baseline config.

** Finding 6: The analytic battery exists in the papers and is headless-portable
- DIRECTGOLib v1.1: 96 box-constrained problems, n ∈ {2,5,10}, known f*, domains; includes Hartman6 (n=6, f*=−3.3223), Goldstein-Price (n=2, f*=3.0), Shekel 5/7/10 (n=4), and n=5 variants of Ackley/Alpine/Griewank/Rastrigin/Rosenbrock/Schwefel/Levy/Michalewicz/Styblinski-Tang — the last being the closest analytic stand-in for 6-DOF pose search. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 Appendix A Table 7; library at https://github.com/blockchain-group/DIRECTGOLib, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6491951]
- GKLS: 8 classes × 100 instances, n ∈ {2,3,4,5}, simple+hard (r or d adjusted); stopping by distance-to-optimum accuracy Δ (eq. 10), budget 1e6 in the study. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §5, Table 5; generator: Gaviano et al., ACM TOMS 29(4):469–480, 2003, DOI 10.1145/962437.962444]
- Scoring convention in the papers: percent-error stop pe = 100·(f−f*)/|f*| (pe=f for f*=0) with ε_pe=1e-2, plus operational-characteristics/data profiles (proportion solved vs budget) — the exact tool for the 20k/35k production budget question. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4; arXiv:2107.02205 §4]
- The repo already has the headless pattern: test/unit/test_direct_optimizer.cpp runs analytic costs (quadratic in 6-D) through DirectOptimizer with budgets 1000–20000, determinism/offset/callback assertions — the natural skeleton for the battery harness. [Source: /home/ajj/repo/uf/JTML/test/unit/test_direct_optimizer.cpp]
- Confidence: high.
- Relevance: the battery spec below is the hand-off to angle 03 (harness owner); this angle owns the variant surface + function/budget/termination choices, not the harness implementation.

* Variant Surface (12 + refinement add-ons)

** Selection schemes
- IO — Improved Original: lower-right convex hull of (size, f(center)) with ε in eq. (4), ties restricted to one candidate per (size,value) group. Current repo = this *without* ε and *with* all ties.
- IA — Improved Aggressive: select the min-value box of every distinct size group, with δ_limit floor (in the study: box subdivided 50n times). Parallel-friendly; worst sequential record in the 2022 study.
- GL — two-step Pareto: step 1 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, f(center) ↓); step 2 Pareto-nondominated on (size ↑, Euclidean distance from x_min ↓); union. No ε, no parameters; "does not have any protection against over-exploration in sub-optimal local minima regions".

** Partitioning schemes
- N-DTC — trisect *all* longest sides at once (2k+1 new evals per POH, k = # of max sides); original DIRECT (Jones 1993).
- 1-DTC — trisect the single longest side only (2 evals per POH); tie-break in the study: least-split-so-far dimension, then lowest index. Repo is 1-DTC-alike but ties break by *denormalized* side length (GetLargestDirection on denormalized sides), lowest index on equality — for anisotropic ranges (branch 15,15,25,25,25,25; leaf 3,3,15,3,3,3) the two rules diverge.
- 1-DTDV — trisect single longest side, sample two *diagonal vertices*; boundary-optimum weapon; catastrophic on interior optima / high n.
- 1-DBDP — bisect along the diagonal, sample two interior diagonal points (reusable across descendants); best n>4 average; needs its own storage/diameter bookkeeping.

** Refinement-control add-ons (on top of GL, per Mathematics 2022)
- -min / -median / -average: ε-style floors f_min−ε|f_min|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_median|, f_min−ε|f_min−f_average| — all hurt, worst at f*=0.
- -limit: δ_limit floor (20n subdivisions in the 2022 paper) + always select the f_min box — hurt slightly (0.7805→0.7631 success).
- -gb: globally-biased two-phase switch (drop local phase after 5 non-improving iterations, security iteration every 5th) — the only non-hurting restriction; best on expensive functions.
- -rev: local phase only on the iteration f_min improves — mixed (best median, 5th success rate).
- ε=0 default in the repo vs ε=1e-4 in DIRECTGO defaults: keep 0 (current behavior) for the analytic battery baseline; the ε>0 option exists for the original-selection regime.

|---------+--------------------------------+-------------------+-------|

| N-DTC-GL | GL family: ~60–72% fewer evals than IO/IA on n>4 | 5th (24,746 avg) | ≡ DIRECT-GL [arXiv:2109.14912 §3] |

| 1-DBDP-GL | best n>4 average (≈16% fewer than N-DTC) | 2nd on simple GKLS at >400 evals; 5th overall | ≡ BIRECT with GL selection [arXiv:2109.14912 §4.1, §5] |

- Budgets/termination (production shape):

  - Crossover probe: 100, 500, 1000, 4000 to confirm the IO→GL regime switch at the exact shapes (papers: IO ≤500, N-DTC-IO ~50% @ 1000–4000, GL ≥4000).
  - Scoring: percent-error stop pe ≤ 1e-2 (f*≠0) / pe=f (f*=0), plus operational-characteristics (proportion solved vs budget) and median-evals-to-solve — same metrics as the papers, so results are directly comparable.

* Recommended default variant for the production budget shape

- Landing variant: **1-DTC-GL-gb** — 1-DTC partition (already the repo's de-facto split rule), GL two-step Pareto selection (n>4, ≥4000-eval regime: ~60–72% fewer evals than IO/IA), locbalance=gb (only refinement control that never hurt; best when evals are expensive — GPU silhouette with dilation 6/3/1). Keep size measure L2 and ε=0 (bit-identical default; no ε-style restrictions — f_min≈0 makes them harmful).
- Stretch variant: 1-DBDP-GL (best n>4 average; needs diagonal-bisection rework of storage/sampling).
- Do not enable 1-DTDV unless the battery (shifted-domain + boundary probes) shows the pose optimum near the range edge; evidence shows it is catastrophic for interior optima.
- Enable the GLh φ-surrogate only if the GPU cost can emit NaN/Inf — this angle could not verify the trigger; that check belongs to angle 02's cost-path audit. If NaN is possible, GLh turns it from silent storage corruption (hull slope NaN) into a feasibility-directed search at near-zero extra cost.
- Ordering per the measurement-first rule: land Options struct with bit-identical defaults first (Tier-1 + Tier-2 gates must stay green on the baseline config), then score 1-DTC-GL vs 1-DTC-GL-gb vs 1-DBDP-GL vs baseline on the battery above; no variant touches production until the harness says so.

* What Could Not Be Verified

#+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

The recommended course of action, in dependency order: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, then behavior-neutral fixes, then the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe on the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (cheapest instrument that sees the z-weak axis) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam; (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json as the scoring surface; (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** (GL two-step Pareto selection + globally-biased refinement control), scored by the harness before any production switch; (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, gated on oracle green and bit-identical cost values; (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06, GO-gated on the z-profile probe and an ablation arm. Architecture work (angle 04) is the enabler that flows through this path as additive cuts A–E rather than a separate project.

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: angle 01's GL recommendation improves search efficiency in 6-D at n>4 budgets (≈60–72% fewer evaluations, high-evidence), but angle 06 shows the 6.31 mm z gap is a magnification observability limit in single-plane fluoro — no selection/partitioning scheme changes what is observable, and a depth channel does not fix it either; the real z remedies are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior, and every z remedy is gated on angle 03's probe. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: angle 05 verified every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results — the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim applies to the DRR float-atomic path, which is not in the DIRECT cost path; a pose→score diff harness makes the bit-identity claim checkable per cut.

The "12x fewer evals" polish thesis should be treated as a target to test, not a justification: angle 06's analysis puts the realistic win at ~1.5–3× in the leaf/refinement phase (trunk 20k dominates the budget), with the chamfer distance-map surrogate as the one smooth gradient signal that exists in the codebase. Everything else from the papers — DIRECT-GLh hidden constraints, 1-DTDV boundary sampling, analytic-AA occlusion gradients, DRR-photometric gradients, torch bridges — is conditional, deferred, or NO-GO per the evidence below, and each lands only through the harness.

** Finding 3 — The literature's highest-evidence algorithm upgrade is 1-DTC-GL-gb, and the current config is the literature's worst local-refinement regime
- Current repo config: original-DIRECT selection, ε=0, selecting ALL hull ties, 1-DTC-alike trisection on the largest denormalized side, L2 size measure. Jones & Martins 2021: ε=0 "spends so many evaluations refining local minima"; the empirical study: tie-all selection increases "global drag". The repo sits exactly in the worst regime the literature documents for a 20k–35k budget. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150; https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912]
- GL (two-step Pareto) selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems; budget crossover: IO wins ≤500 evals, N-DTC-IO best ~1000–4000, GL best ≥4000 — the 6-DOF search at 20k trunk lives far above the crossover. Partitioning: 1-DBDP best n>4 average but needs diagonal-bisection rework; 1-DTC best GKLS median and minimal code change; 1-DTDV catastrophic for interior optima (141,999 evals vs 919 on Levy10) — a trap unless the pose optimum is confirmed near the range boundary. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 2; https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.1–4.2, Table 3]
- Refinement control (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760): every restriction except -gb hurts 1-DTC-GL on 287 DIRECTGOLib problems; -gb is the only one that never hurt and is best on expensive objectives (GPU silhouette with dilation 6/4/1 renders is expensive). Restrictions hurt worst when f* ≈ 0 — the silhouette-cost shape. ε-style restrictions are doubly contraindicated (the ε|f_min| window collapses as f_min→0). Landing variant: **1-DTC-GL-gb**, ε=0, L2 size kept, bit-identical defaults preserved behind an Options struct. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 4; https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf §3–§4]
- DIRECT-GLh (φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate for infeasible/NaN points) is near-zero cost — the distances are already computed by GL's two-step selection — and beats barrier/NAS methods 18/80 vs 29–53/80 failures on hidden-constraint problems. But the trigger is unverified: no finite-check exists anywhere in the C++ cost path, so whether the production GPU cost can emit NaN is unknown; angle 02's cost-path audit owns that check, and GLh is conditional on it. Today a NaN result poisons hull slope comparisons in ConvexHull (silent storage corruption). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 3; https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02205 §2.3, §4.2.1]

** Finding 4 — The z-weak axis is an observability limit, not an algorithm problem; the probe is the arbiter, and the real remedies are biplane or a known-geometry prior
- The 6.31 mm z gap (vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane) is the run's load-bearing research problem, converged from prior runs. The mechanism: a z shift is pure magnification — at ~1.1 m source distance a ±15 mm shift changes scale by <1%, inside the 6 px dilation tolerance; the dilated-overlap family is nearly flat in z. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "z-profile probe"; local-recon.org]
- The z-profile probe reuses the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+): sweep Δz ∈ {−15,…,+15} mm at fixed truth for the other 5 axes, 31 cost calls per (variant, dilation, frame) — a couple of minutes total on the RTX 3090 — and report valley_depth = (max−cost(0))/(max−min). A z-blind metric shows a flat or off-center curve. This is the cheapest instrument that sees the z-weak axis, and it gates every z remedy (SAME_Z weight calibration, chamfer reweighting, leaf refinement). [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "z-profile probe"]
- Angle 06's verdict on the depth channel: the machinery is ~80% present (DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z; dev_z_line_values_ buffer exists), but a front-surface z/w buffer does NOT make z observable in single-plane fluoro — there is no target depth to compare against, the gap is the magnification limit (no gradient changes what is observable), and NVDiffrast intentionally does not backprop through z/w (issue #70). The depth machinery is worth it only as: occlusion-aware visibility gradients, a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm, or the z-line-integral in the ML/DRR pathway. The real z fixes are biplane (calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B + biplane branch already exist) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone) — matching the prior-run ML angle's finding 8. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "depth channel"; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70]
- This is the dispatch-requested contradiction flag: angle 01's variant recommendations (1-DTC-GL-gb) optimize search efficiency but cannot move the z gap — the two are different kinds of improvement, and the probe is the instrument that separates them. A variant-switch win on the harness must not be mistaken for a z fix.

** Finding 5 — The cost path is sync-bound (structurally confirmed, magnitude unmeasured); 3 of 5 D2H syncs are trivially async-able, and int-atomics make bit-identical results achievable
- Per monoplane eval: ~15 kernel launches (8 render + 4 fast-implant-dilation + 3 distance-map) + 5 synchronous D2H cudaMemcpy, all on the default stream, zero streams/events anywhere in src/. The 5 syncs classify as: 2 structural mid-eval (bounding box at render_engine.cu:781–785; fragment_fill at :786–790 — removable only via kernel-level change) and 3 terminal (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289–290; distance_map_metric.cu:110–114, :115–119) — async-able now, all targets already page-locked. Cost nuance: the pairs share drains, so the real exposure is ~3 host-block windows per eval. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "Sync-point inventory"]
- The existing ms/call meter (optimizer_manager.cpp:1272–1278) uses clock() = process CPU time: it excludes GPU time AND sync-wait time, so it systematically under-reads a sync-bound pipeline and cannot arbitrate the item-8 claim. Fixing the meter (Cut 4) is required before any cut can be demonstrated to the user via the UI. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "The ms/call meter"]
- Determinism: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd/atomicSub on single counters — integer addition is order-independent, so identical launch configs + inputs ⇒ bit-identical scores. This resolves the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim: it applies to the DRR float-atomic path, which is NOT in the DIRECT cost path. Consequence: async terminal copies and iteration batching can be verified bit-identical by diffing a recorded pose→score sequence; Cut 3 (fragment-fill removal) must preserve per-thread work for threads < fragment_fill exactly. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "Determinism"]
- The DIRECT loop is sequential but each iteration's evals are pairwise independent (TrisectPotentiallyOptimal evaluates 2×N centers from a pre-loop snapshot) — batchable with replay-ordered bookkeeping, no GPU kernel rewrite. Constraint: FastImplantDilationMetric writes INTO the rendered buffer, so evals must be double-buffered (second render output + duplicate score buffers); biplane gets a free overlap (secondary camera buffers are separate). [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "The DIRECT loop is sequential", "In-place metric composition"]
- nvtx: declared in pixi.toml, zero instrumentation, and -DLIBNVTOOLSEXT is dead config; the nvtx3 header-only API compiles with no CMake/link change (toolkit include path already on jtml_compute). nsight-compute is in the lock; nsight-systems is not (needs pixi add). Per-eval timing data from Cut 0 replaces angle 03's derived 20–60 evals/s estimate. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "nvtx", "Measurement protocol"]

** Finding 6 — The polish stage is feasible only on a smooth surrogate; GO for chamfer-gradient polish, NO-GO for photometric/torch routes; the "12x" thesis is likely overstated
- The production DIRECT_DILATION cost is piecewise-constant in pose (binary silhouette + int reductions): finite differences on it give zero/garbage Jacobians; there is no gradient to polish through it. The surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a mean-chamfer loss with a Lipschitz image-space gradient ∇D, and its analytic gradient is the standard silhouette gradient dL/dθ = Σ ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ), needing only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics FillTriangleKernel already computes and discards (~10 lines + one float4 buffer to stage them). Published relatives: arXiv:1906.07870, arXiv:2501.14918. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "piecewise-constant", "smooth surrogate"]
- Feasibility verdicts: silhouette-gradient polish on the chamfer surrogate — GO (MVP = forward differences, 6 renders/step ~1 week; then analytic Jacobian + ∇D kernel, 1 render/step, +1 week; reuses Render(), uploaded distance maps, injected-cost lambda; float accumulation; match production backface=true and leaf dilation 1). NDC z/w depth buffer — feasible machinery but NOT a z fix; only as occlusion/ablation enabler. Analytic AA / occlusion-aware gradients — research increment after the MVP shows a win. Photometric DRR-intensity gradient — NO-GO for now (+3–6 weeks, low expected value). Finite-difference on the production cost — NO-GO. Torch bridge — NO-GO on design merit (autograd buys nothing for a 6-DoF static-STL scatter-add backward; and torch is already linked into jtml_compute — the ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is a smell flagged to angle 04). [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "Feasibility verdicts"]
- Hybrid loop: trunk 20k → 2×branch 5k → leaf 5k → RunPolishStage(current_optimum) → optional DIRECT re-seed around the polished pose (Gablonsky locally-biased DIRECT / DIRECT+DF-local-search literature). Plug-in point mirrors RunDirectStage, no OptimizerRunLaunch signature change (reuses the leaf CostFunctionManager), budget-accounted (every surrogate + verification eval increments cost_function_calls_ so DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish is apples-to-apples at equal cumulative budget). Deliberately NOT routed through the Stage enum — the always-Trunk guard bug makes it unreliable. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "hybrid loop"]
- The "~12x fewer evals" thesis: unverified and structurally suspect — the budget is trunk-dominated (20k of 35k), so a 12x total claim requires shrinking the trunk (the ML-initializer pathway's job), while a gradient method plausibly converges the leaf refinement (~10^2 steps on a smooth surrogate) several-fold faster. Realistic expectation to measure: ~1.5–3× on the leaf phase + tighter final accuracy + lower frame-to-frame variance, at equal cumulative budget, reported data-profile style. GO condition for production: ablation arm shows ≥ the IoU gate at equal-or-lower cumulative budget with no per-axis regression; precondition: the z-profile probe shows the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "12x thesis", "go/no-go"]

** Finding 7 — The backend seam evolution is additive-first and deliberately minimal: payload + StageScript + named derivations, no new layer
- The "backend" is already a stack of three seams (OptimizerRunDriver, Optimize()'s stage loop, DirectOptimizer's injected std::function). The target shape: OptimizerRunLaunch stays the single by-value payload, additively gaining the DIRECT Options struct; the stage sequence becomes a StageScript (vector of StageSpec: {kind, range, budget, repeat, cfm_index}) that the same Optimize() executor consumes; dilation/dark-silhouette derivation (DeriveStageCostParams) and the cost-adapter construction (BuildGpuCostAdapter) become named pure functions; DirectOptimizer's boundary stays std::function<double(const Point6D&)>. Explicitly NO RunBackend enum (the driver IS the run-level backend — the fake driver proves it), NO new CMake target, NO headless executor extraction until the multi-stage oracle demonstrates the driver seam insufficient, NO ML in the loop. [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "Target shape", "non-goals"]
- Dilation stays COST-owned: it is a derived property of the active CFM parameters (the "Dilation"/"dark_silhouette" name scan at optimizer_manager.cpp:237–345), not optimizer config — moving it would fork the single source of truth. The seam is the named pure function DeriveStageCostParams, called once in Initialize. This deliberately counters the dispatch's "dilation under optimizer configuration" framing. [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "Dilation stays COST-owned"]
- Payload evolution contract: additive fields are FREE (DirectOptimizer::Options defaulted = today's behavior; the fake-driver test records the whole launch by value and compiles unchanged); restructuring into nested sections is ONE gated signature-adaptation cut with the test updated in the same change; the driver interface, Initialize signature, by-value forwarding, the 8 binds, and the epoch/threadActive gate never change. Do NOT move the 3 CFMs to pointers (perf decision pending measurement; would change the fake-driver copy semantics). [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "Payload evolution contract"]
- The stage loop stays in Optimize() and becomes script-driven in place: the loop is the only algorithm policy among three interleaved work kinds (session/GPU state and signal emission stay in the manager). RunDirectStage stays the stage runner; its injected lambda becomes BuildGpuCostAdapter, with three consumers converging on it (production runner, z-profile probe, and oracle_test's hand-rolled twin at oracle_test.cpp:286–291). A future gradient-polish stage is one StageSpec + one new StageKind + its own runner branch — same seam, no StageRunner interface built today. R13 gap honestly recorded: Optimize()'s loop has no headless emission-order pin today (manager is GPU-bound); Cut B's evidence is parity + oracle green + jj diff relocation + the new pure-function pins. [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "script-driven loop", "R13 pin surface", "Migration sketch"]

- Not a factual disagreement but a scoping tension the user must hold: angle 01's GL/1-DTC-GL-gb upgrade is about search efficiency at n>4, ≥4000-eval budgets — it changes which poses are tried, not what the cost can observe. ** Contradiction 3 — Perf cuts vs determinism: the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim vs the verified int-atomic cost path
- Angle 05 verified every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd/atomicSub (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:145,147; distance_map_metric.cu:46–47; gpu_metrics.cu:129; iou.cu:66–72) — integer addition is order-independent, so results ARE bit-reproducible given identical launch configs and inputs. The order-nondeterministic float atomicAdd lives in the DRR fill (render_drr_engine.cu), which is NOT in the DIRECT cost path. Resolution: the docs' claim is stale; the determinism twin is a pose→score diff harness, and every perf cut (async copies, batching) is gated on the diff being empty. The one cut with a real determinism caveat is Cut 3 (fragment-fill kernel change), which must preserve per-thread work for threads < fragment_fill exactly. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "Determinism"; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "ablation.json — determinism semantics"]

** Contradiction 4 — Backface culling: production ON vs oracle/label-generator OFF
- Production OptimizerManager constructs GPUModel with use_backface_culling=true; every oracle/parity path and the Study2Grid label generator use false (in-source comment: "BACKFACE CULLING APPEARS TO BE GIVING ERRORS"). The oracle must stay OFF: labels were generated OFF, and the frame↔label correspondence is pinned empirically by start-pose render IoU == 1.0 only under OFF; switching the oracle would break the gate against OFF-generated labels. The measured 0.9936 is an OFF-vs-OFF number and self-consistent. For production, ON is defensible for a closed opaque implant, but the two paths render different silhouette conventions where the STL is open/concave. Recommended evidence before touching production: (a) headless manifoldness check on KR_right_7_fem.stl (boundary edges == 0 ⇒ closed), (b) GPU-labeled ON-vs-OFF silhouette IoU at the golden pose (≈1.0 ⇒ immaterial; measurably <1 ⇒ deliberate reconciliation needed). Angle 06's polish must match the production backface config (true) for verification consistency — itself a tension with the oracle's OFF pin. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, "Backface divergence"; angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "Feasibility verdicts"]

- torch is already linked into jtml_compute (machine_learning_tools.cpp is in the lib; CostFunctionManager.h includes <ATen/ops/div_native.h>) yet angle 06 says NO-GO on a torch bridge for polish (autograd buys nothing for the scatter-add backward; violates the "no torch in the cost path" design). ** Contradiction 6 — "12x fewer evals" (user's thesis) vs angle 06's ~1.5–3× leaf-phase estimate
- The thesis is unverified and structurally implausible as a total-budget claim: the trunk (20k of 35k cumulative) dominates, and polish cannot shrink the global phase. The honest target: evals-to-target-IoU at equal cumulative budget, data-profile style, with the win concentrated in leaf refinement. This is not a dispute about facts — it is the run's one explicitly low-confidence claim, to be arbitrated by the ablation arm. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "12x thesis"]

** Contradiction 7 — Split tie-break: repo (largest denormalized side) vs study (least-split-so-far)
- Angle 01: the repo's 1-DTC-alike rule ties break on the denormalized side length; the 2022 study's 1-DTC ties break least-split-so-far then lowest index. For anisotropic branch/leaf ranges (15,15,25,25,25,25; 3,3,15,3,3,3) the rules diverge; the effect on the 6-DOF search is unquantified. The battery should include an anisotropic-range probe using the actual trunk/branch/leaf ranges as box bounds. This is a mechanical-difference flag, not a correctness dispute — the repo's behavior is the pinned baseline either way.
